paper_metadata.title: Tailoring the Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Ti1.5NbZrV0.4Mo0.6 High Entropy Alloy via C and Si Doping

evidence.quote: the individual effects of C element (Ti1.5NbZrV0.4Mo0.6Cx, x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, molar ratios), and the synergistic effects of C and Si (Ti1.5NbZrV0.4Mo0.6(SiC)y, y = 0.5 and 1.0, molar ratios) on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Ti1.5NbZrV0.4Mo0.6 alloy are systematically explored.
The co-doping of C and Si generates a complex microstructure composed of body centered cubic phase, carbides, and silicides
The alloys prepared using graphite powder and silicon particles to introduce C and Si elements separately were termed Spr A0.5 and Spr A1
The alloys prepared using graphite powder and silicon particles to introduce C and Si elements separately were termed Spr A0.5 and Spr A1
those that introduced nonmetallic elements simultaneously through SiC particles were termed Smt A0.5 and Smt A1
those that introduced nonmetallic elements simultaneously through SiC particles were termed Smt A0.5 and Smt A1

alloy ingots were prepared by vacuum nonconsumable arc melting using high purity (>99.95%) Mo, Nb, Ti, V, and Zr metal particles and graphite powder; polysilicon particles; and SiC powder as raw materials. Each ingot had been melted at least five times to make the composition uniform.
As observed in the figure, both the BCC phase and the MC (where M represents metal elements such as Zr, Nb, Ti, etc.) carbide phase are present.

These second-phase peaks can be attributed to the MC (M represents metal elements such as Zr, Nb, Ti, etc.) carbide phase and the M5Si3 (M represents metal elements such as Zr, Nb, Ti, etc.) silicide phase.
The microstructure of the alloys consists of a BCC-solid solution and carbide phases. The morphology of the carbides and BCC phase changes significantly with varying carbon content.
